units.text: ⟦0⟧ prints two kinds of messages: diagnostic messages (errors and warnings) written to standard error and help messages written to standard output. Diagnostic messages may be suppresed with option ⟦1⟧. Help messages may be enabled with option ⟦2⟧ and may be toggled with command ‘⟦3⟧’.
units.sourceHTML: ed prints two kinds of messages: diagnostic messages (errors and warnings) written to standard error and help messages written to standard output. Diagnostic messages may be suppresed with option -q. Help messages may be enabled with option -v and may be toggled with command ‘H’.

units.text: ⟦0⟧ warns the first time that a command modifies a buffer loaded from a read-only file.
units.sourceHTML: ed warns the first time that a command modifies a buffer loaded from a read-only file.

units.text: When an error occurs, if ⟦0⟧’s standard input is a regular file or here document, then it exits, otherwise it prints a ‘⟦1⟧’ and returns to command mode. An explanation of the last error can be printed with the ‘⟦2⟧’ (help) command.
units.sourceHTML: When an error occurs, if ed’s standard input is a regular file or here document, then it exits, otherwise it prints a ‘?’ and returns to command mode. An explanation of the last error can be printed with the ‘h’ (help) command.

units.text: If the ‘⟦0⟧’ (undo) command occurs in a global command list, then the command list is executed only once.
units.sourceHTML: If the ‘u’ (undo) command occurs in a global command list, then the command list is executed only once.
